name: KaitenCode
shortDescription: Tauri desktop app that runs AI coding agents on a kanban board, with columns as pipeline stages that fire triggers, terminals and PRs.
description:
KaitenCode (formerly bento-ya) is a Tauri desktop app for orchestrating AI coding agents on an automated kanban board. Each column is a pipeline stage with optional `on_entry` / `on_exit` triggers: describe the automation in natural language and the app generates the trigger config, or use the advanced editor for actions like `spawn_cli`, `move_column`, `run_script` and `create_pr`.

Highlights:
- Per-task agent panel: semantic transcript, a tmux-backed terminal, lifecycle controls (Hold / Stop / Kill), model and thinking-effort selectors, and a chat box for steering the agent mid-run.
- v2.0: GitHub PR auto-create on column exit, per-task git worktree isolation, and a task-dependency DAG with cycle detection and hover-reveal bezier lines.
- v2.1: a full xterm.js terminal per task (WebGL renderer, 10k-line scrollback, Unicode 11, theme-reactive) with lazy PTY sessions and persistent tmux sessions.
- A localhost-only HTTP API with a per-run bearer token powers an MCP server, so external agents can drive the board.
- Tested in three modes: browser/Vite with mocked IPC, native Tauri, and native WebDriver E2E against the real binary.
